defect: Two distinct questions carry id=Q263: a 27th-BCS item (বাংলাদেশে সর্বপ্রথম কোন মহিলা টেস্টটিউব শিশুর মা হন?, topic বাংলাদেশের জনতত্ত্ব) and a 35th-BCS item (সপ্তম পঞ্চবার্ষিক পরিকল্পনা কোন মেয়াদে হবে?, topic বাংলাদেশের অর্থনীতি). They are unrelated questions from different exams, not a duplicated row.
impact: Any join on _corpus_id returns two rows for Q263 and would attach one fact's provenance to the other. Checked: no such join exists. resource_corpus.py and verify_temporal_corpus.py each read _corpus_id in exactly one place, both times copying it into an output row as a label; every join in the workflow keys on fact_uid, which is unique across all 616 facts. Both facts remain intact and distinct.
downstream_note: In every one of these the corpus_id sits next to the fact_uid that produced it, so the row is identifiable regardless of the collision and no artifact needs to be discarded. They do need regenerating after any renumbering, so that the label matches the source again.
not_done: No ID was rewritten and no fact was dropped (rules 11 and 12). validate() reports this as a standing warning rather than resolving it.
proposed_fix: Fix upstream in bcs_questions_corpus.json: renumber the occurrence that sorts SECOND in file order -- the 35th-BCS five-year-plan item -- to Q498 (the current max id is Q497; gaps at Q214, Q215, Q401 and Q439 are deliberately left alone rather than back-filled, so the id stays monotonic with insertion order). Then re-derive _corpus_id for BCSGK-0386 and regenerate the artifacts listed above. This is a source-corpus edit and needs PI sign-off.
why_the_second_occurrence: File order is the only non-arbitrary tiebreak available here, and renumbering the second keeps the first occurrence's label stable. Neither choice orphans anything, since every downstream reference is recoverable through fact_uid.
